subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Puerperium: involution, sepsis, breastfeeding and contraception timing

steps.tx: **Uterine involution** completes by 6 weeks as the fundus falls from the umbilicus on day one by a finger breadth daily. **Afterpains** trouble multiparous and breastfeeding mothers as oxytocin contracts the uterus during feeds. **Lochia** progresses from red rubra in the first week through serosa to alba, while a boggy fundus needs massage and retained tissue needs exploration. Fever above 38 on two readings beyond the first 24 hours, with tachycardia or hypotension, warns of sepsis. Early catheter removal and fibre rich diet restore bladder and bowel function.
steps.say: The uterus shrinks daily from the navel and is back to size by six weeks. Afterpains grip multiparous mothers during feeds because suckling releases oxytocin. Lochia is red at first, then turns brownish and pale over weeks. A boggy fundus needs massage while persistent fever with fast pulse warns of infection.

steps.tx: **Puerperal sepsis** spans **endometritis** with fever, uterine tenderness and foul lochia, plus wound infection, mastitis, urinary infection and thrombophlebitis after prolonged rupture or caesarean section. Group A streptococcus can trigger toxic shock, so blood cultures precede broad **gentamicin with clindamycin** cover. **Septic pelvic thrombophlebitis** hides behind fever that spikes despite antibiotics and responds to a heparin trial. Necrotising fasciitis declares itself through pain out of proportion and needs urgent debridement, while hand hygiene bundles prevent many cases.
steps.say: Puerperal sepsis follows prolonged rupture and operative birth with fever and a tender uterus. Foul discharge points to the uterine lining while red wounds, hot breasts and burning urine reveal other sources. Cultures must precede broad antibiotics so therapy stays targeted. Fever that spikes despite drugs suggests clotted pelvic veins and earns a heparin trial.

steps.tx: The illustration shows a sagittal pelvis with an inflamed endometrial cavity, a tender **subinvoluted uterus** under a palpating hand, and **purulent lochia** draining through the vagina. **Endometritis** causes fever with uterine tenderness and foul discharge after prolonged rupture or section, and it needs cultures before gentamicin with clindamycin. For the exam, link tenderness plus foul lochia to the uterine lining rather than to wound, breast or urine sources. Persistent spikes despite antibiotics point toward septic pelvic thrombophlebitis.
steps.say: The diagram cuts through the pelvis and exposes an inflamed uterine cavity. A gloved hand presses a bulky tender uterus while foul pus drains below. Fever with tenderness and smelly discharge identifies endometritis after birth. Cultures should precede antibiotics, and spikes that persist despite drugs suggest clotted pelvic veins.

steps.tx: **Colostrum** feeds the newborn for the first days before mature milk arrives around week two, given on demand in 8 to 12 feeds with an asymmetric **latch** that takes in areola. **Mastitis** shows a wedge of erythema with fever and needs flucloxacillin while nursing continues, whereas a **breast abscess** needs drainage alongside continued feeding and engorgement eases with cold cabbage leaves. Cracked nipples heal when latch corrects, most medicines stay compatible though tetracyclines and codeine stay banned, and suppressed HIV on treatment allows nursing.
steps.say: Colostrum is the first milk that nourishes the baby for the first days before mature milk flows. Frequent on demand feeds with a deep asymmetric latch protect supply and nipples. A hot wedge with fever signals mastitis, and it needs antibiotics while feeds continue. Abscesses need drainage, but nursing should persist because continued emptying heals the breast.

steps.tx: The **lactational amenorrhoea method** protects exclusively breastfeeding mothers under 6 months with 98 percent efficacy. An **intrauterine device** fits immediately after placental delivery, progestin methods stay safe during nursing, combined pills wait until 6 months of nursing or 3 weeks without nursing because of clot risk, and sterilisation remains available. **Postnatal visits** on day 3, weeks one to two and 6 weeks screen mood with the Edinburgh scale, correct anaemia with iron and start perineal exercises. Rubella vaccine and anti D complete care, with 18 months before the next conception.
steps.say: Exclusive nursing without periods protects mothers for six months with high efficacy. Intrauterine devices and progestin methods suit nursing mothers while combined pills wait because of clot risk. Scheduled reviews check mood, blood counts and pelvic healing in turn. Vaccines and anti D are needed to finish care while families plan a healthy gap.
